 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Sambasiva Rao Naidu

Judgment :

Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This appeal has been filed by the appellants who are petitioner Nos.1 to 3 in O.P.No.766 of 2003 on the file of I Additional District Judge-cum-Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Nalgonda,
assailing the judgment and award in the above referred petition by which the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.2,43,646/- with costs and future interest @ 7.5% from the date of petition till the amount was realized.

The petitioners who have filed O.P.No.766 of 2003 claiming an amount of Rs.11,00,000/- on account of death of one Nashaboina Rama Chandraiah (hereinafter be referred to as deceased), having not satisfied with the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal preferred this appeal under Section 173 of M.V.Act., on the following grounds:
The Tribunal committed grave error by awarding meager amount of compensation and failed to appreciate oral and documentary evidence produced by the appellants herein.

The appellants have claimed that the Tribunal ought to have considered the salary of the deceased while calculating the compensation amount and as the deceased was below 30 years ought to have added 30% of the income of the deceased towards future prospects.

They have also claimed that the Tribunal ought to have allowed the petition by granting compensation in view of the pain and suffering and also because of loss of love and affection due to the death of the deceased.
2. The appellants have claimed that Court below ought not to have taken a lenient view while awarding compensation in a fatal accident case.
The appellants have claimed that the Court below ought to have applied multiplier of 15, because the age of the deceased was 49 years at the time of accident, which resulted his death.
3. The appeal is filed against the judgment in O.P.No.766 of 2003 which in fact, was decided on 09.01.2006.
The appellants have filed this appeal with interlocutory application vide I.A.No.2 of 2021 with a prayer to condone the delay of (5397) days in filing the appeal.
After hearing both parties, the said application was allowed by this Court on condition that the petitioners are not entitled to interest for the above referred period.

4. As could be seen from the award and material averments of the petition filed before the Tribunal,
it shows that the deceased was working as Head Constable at Yadagirigutta Police Station.

On 11.08.2003, while he was proceeding from Vangapally on a motor bike of another constable to enquire about passport particulars and while they were on the way, a tanker bearing No.TN-21-A-3555 which came in opposite direction, dashed the bike by overtaking another auto and Nashboina Saidamma And 2 Others vs B. sentences.text: Even though he was immediately shifted to Government Hospital, Bhongiri, he succumbed to the injuries on the same day.
The rider of the bike also suffered injuries in the said accident.
A case was registered by police, Bhongiri and subsequently, charge sheet was filed against the driver of the tanker.

5. The petitioners who are wife, children, grand daughter and parents of the deceased, filed the above referred original petition against the driver and owner of the vehicle and also against the insurance company from which the policy was obtained against the above said tanker.
6. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 remained exparte.
The insurance company contested the petition, filed counter disputing the material averments made by the petitioners.
During enquiry, the 1st petitioner was examined as PW1.
Petitioner Nos.2 to 7 were also examined on their behalf.
Ex. A1
to A12 were marked.
The contesting respondent did not adduce any oral evidence, but marked a copy of policy as Ex.B1.

The Tribunal having considered the oral and documentary evidence, allowed the petition in part by awarding compensation of Rs.2,43,646/- with proportionate cost and interest @ 7.5% by fixing the liability against all the respondents.
7. Heard both parties.

8. Now the point for consideration is :
Whether there are grounds to enhance compensation, as prayed for?

9. POINT:
As already stated, the original petition was filed in the year 2003 and the accident that took place on 11.08.2003, nearly 20 years lapsed since the date of accident.
Though (8) petitioners have filed the above petition, except petitioner Nos.1 to 3, the remaining petitioners are not added as parties to the present appeal.
As per the description in the petition, the remaining petitioners are shown as children, grand daughter and parents of the deceased.

10. In view of the lapse of 20 years, it is deemed that either the remaining petitioners lost interest in the petition or the remaining children of the deceased must have attained majority and there is no explanation in the petition whether the parents of the deceased are still alive.
Therefore, it is decided that the claim of the petitioners is restricted to appellant Nos.1 to 3 only.
The accident occurred in which the deceased succumbed to injuries and later died in the hospital is not in dispute.

Similarly,
there is no dispute about the employment of the deceased as constable in police department.
The age of the deceased was shown as 45 years which is also not in serious dispute.
The petitioners have claimed that the deceased was in the promotion list as Assistant Sub Inspector with a left over service of 13 years.
According to the evidence placed before the Court, the deceased was working as Head Constable.
PW5 who was working as Superintendent in D.P.O. Nalgonda deposed before the Court that the deceased was working as Head Constable and attached to District Special Branch Police, Nalgonda.

As per the evidence of PW5, the salary of the deceased was Rs.8,812/- and the net Nashboina Saidamma And 2 Others vs B. Thimmappa And 7 Others on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80493705/

sentences.text: 2 salary was Rs.8,197/- per month.
11. As rightly contended by the counsel, the Court below did not consider the future prospects of the deceased.
Even though there are some deductions as noticed by the trial Court, the net salary of the deceased was admittedly Rs.8,197/-.

Since the age of the deceased was 45 years, he appellants are entitled to claim excess compensation in view of the Judgment in National Insurance Company vs.
Praynay Sethi.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company vs.
Praynay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellants are entitled to an additional 25% of the admitted income of the deceased as future prospects.
The same was not considered by the Court below.
12. The Tribunal while calculating the compensation, considered the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.2,427.80.

As per the evidence of PW5 the total salary of the deceased was Rs.8,812/-
and net salary was Rs.8,197/-.

As per the cross examination of PW5 it shows that out of the said amount, the deceased received net salary of Rs.2,427/- after deductions of GPF, APGLI, festival Advance, Group Insurance, Profession Tax and Non-Government deductions.
The Court below,

while considering the net income of the deceased as income, committed an error and failed to consider the above deductions are nothing but savings of the deceased, to which the family members of the deceased are entitled to receive.
An amount of Rs.7,900/- is shown as total deductions.

Out of the said amount, Rs.3,188/- is shown as Bhadratha loan and Rs.1,112/- is shown PCS loan, Rs.100/-
towards PCS fund and Rs.50/- is shown as Aarogya Bhadratha.
Therefore, the Court below could not have deducted the amounts or could have calculated the same as income of the deceased.
13. Therefore, if the net salary of the deceased is considered as Rs.6,000/- per month, still the claimants are entitled to an additional 30% towards future prospects.
In view of the age of the deceased he has got not less than 12 or 13 years of service.

Therefore, if 30% is added the monthly income of the deceased would be Rs.7,800/- and if  of the amount i.e., Rs.1,950/- is deducted towards his personal expenses, the monthly contribution would be Rs.5,850/- and that it is Rs.70,200/- per year.
Even if the age of the deceased is considered as 49, the multiplier to be applied is (14).
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled to Rs.9,82,800/- (Rs.5,850x12=70,200 and 70,200x14).
In addition to this the petitioners/claimants are entitled to Rs.15000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.

Therefore,
another sum of Rs.70,000/- shall be added to the compensation.
14. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by granting Rs.10,52,800/- as compensation.
The appellants are entitled to receive the balance amount, but they are not entitled to any interest on the enhanced compensation in view of the delay in filing the appeal.
As a sequel, pending Miscellaneous Applications, if any, shall stand closed.
